title: Fig and Sherry Pan Sauce
description: Soft figs and dry sherry give this beef-broth reduction a deep fruit flavor that suits sliced filet or pork tenderloin.
equipment: Immersion blender and tall heatproof jug

ingredients.name: dried figs
ingredients.note: Remove hard stems before weighing and chop finely.

steps.title: Soften the figs
steps.text: Melt {butter} in the HexClad over medium-low heat. Stir in {figs} for 2 minutes until glossy and fragrant.

steps.title: Deglaze the skillet
steps.text: Pour in {sherry} off heat. Return to medium and scrape up the browned fig sugars while the sherry bubbles for 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer until tender
steps.text: Add {broth} and {pepper}. Cover and simmer for 8–10 minutes until the fig pieces crush easily.

steps.title: Smooth the reduction
steps.text: Puree the figs and cooking liquid in the deep jug. Press through a fine sieve into the skillet to catch the seeds.

steps.title: Stir the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Stir in the freshly mixed slurry and cook for about 1 minute, whisking until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the finished sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 1/2 cups total. If it measures short, whisk in a little hot water. If it measures over, return it to the skillet and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon a warm pool under thinly sliced filet or pork, then ladle more between the slices.

notes: Yield: 1 1/2 cups. One serving is 1/4 cup. Make ahead: The fig and sherry base can be cooked and strained one day ahead. Thicken it shortly before dinner. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze in quarter-cup portions for up to 2 months. The fruit puree helps the gravy come together again. Fridge reheat: Bring a portion to a boil in a small pan, stirring until it reaches at least 165°F. Loosen with a little water as needed. Freezer reheat: Thaw in the refrigerator overnight and reheat as for a chilled portion. Option A uses dry sherry and black pepper. For gentler Option B, replace the sherry with additional beef broth and omit the pepper. Use avocado oil in place of butter for a dairy-free sauce. Nutrition counts the full measured wine before reduction. Evaporation can lower the calories in the finished sauce. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/6 of recipe): 49 kcal, 1.3 g protein, 7.0 g total carbohydrate, 0.7 g fat, 0.7 g fiber, 17 mg sodium. The estimate covers the prepared condiment. Add separately served foods when totaling a meal. Fiber is estimated before straining.
